description: s441 round 4 control. A handler with an awaited server call and an inner `(event) => …` parameter and a block-local `const event` (different bindings) compiles: the event poisoning follows the handler's event BINDING (scope-resolved), not the name, and applies only after the first await. (s457 3a: the handler takes the event as the parameter of a `${(event) => { … }}` listener — a compiler-wrapped handler does not bind `event`, SPEC §5.2.)
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 10 (g-boot-event-cases-unhandled-server-call-s478)
rationale: §13.2: the rule concerns the handler's own event parameter after its first await; other bindings named `event`, and uses before the await, are unaffected. (S478 open-Qs ruling item 10: the server call is written as a handled statement — `const ok: bool = isOk(1) !{ _ :> false };` then `@verdict = ok ? … : …;` — since §19.9.10 makes an unhandled client call of a server function E-ERROR-002; the case's point is unchanged.)
